meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have on the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People write in a notes app and paste it in, so where's the draft he pasted from?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Then whatever happens next stays off his record, and it stays between us and Owen.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time. A bad citation isn't cheating, Hale.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Whatever you put on the table, it isn't in front of his class, and nothing goes in his file. I want that in writing.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines exist so students can change their minds. That's what a thesis does between drafts.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, before December 1, and it never goes near his class. Nothing on his record, Hale.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check his shifts tonight. Put Thursday in the email, and the time.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite for Owen, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that promise in writing, along with the confirmed day and time for the rewrite. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1, and she still wants the written promise that nothing goes on his record and a confirmed time; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasted-draft defence by offering to look at any dated draft, because it was specific, dated and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the gradebook mistake up front and never attacked Owen or leaned on the detector.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing near midnight on a late October night, very close to what she was hiding, and while that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said outlines exist so students can change their minds, answer that point before offering 4.4, for example by saying the rewrite will let Owen explain the shift from cowardice to his new argument himself.
